title: What Is Meta App Manager? Why It's on Your Phone and Whether to Delete It
summary: Meta App Manager is an Android system app that installs and updates Facebook apps. What it does, why it is on your phone, how to disable it, and how it differs from Ads Manager.
body_markdown:
## The short answer


- **Meta App Manager** is a system app on many Android phones, formerly called Facebook App Manager. It installs, updates and manages Meta's apps, such as Facebook, Messenger and Instagram.
- It is not the same as **Meta Ads Manager** , the website advertisers use to run ads. If you came here looking for that, skip to the section on the difference.
- It is preinstalled by the phone maker or carrier, so you often cannot uninstall it. You can usually **disable** it in Settings.
- Disabling it is safe for most people. Your Meta apps keep working and update through the Google Play Store.
- If you do not use Facebook, Instagram or Messenger at all, disabling it also removes a background app that has no use for you.


People find Meta App Manager in their app list, in a battery or data usage screen, or in a permissions prompt, and wonder why a company they never signed up with has software on their phone. Here is what it is, what it does, and what to do about it.


## What it is


Meta App Manager is a small Android system service from Meta, the company behind Facebook and Instagram. It was introduced as Facebook App Manager and renamed when the company became Meta. It comes from preinstallation deals, where Meta has arrangements with some phone makers and mobile carriers to ship its apps on new phones.


It is an Android thing. iPhones do not have it.


## Why it is on your phone


The main reason is distribution. If Facebook and Instagram arrive with the phone, more people use them. Meta App Manager is the part that keeps those preinstalled apps installed and current, and it can take care of installing other Meta apps without you going through the Play Store each time.


Depending on your phone, it is bundled with related components that may appear in your app list under names such as Meta Services and Meta App Installer. Together they form a package that supports the Meta apps already on the device.


## What it does


- Installs and updates Meta apps on the device.
- Supports communication between Meta apps, such as logging into one with another's account.
- May run in the background to support those functions.


Meta describes the app as a tool for managing its apps. It does not give any extra features to you, the user, that you would notice day to day.


## Is it safe?


It is not malware. It is real software from Meta, signed and included by your phone's maker. That does not make it harmless to everyone, and reasonable people disagree on it:


- **Privacy.** It is a background app from a company whose business is advertising, and it holds system-level permissions. If you do not use Meta's apps, you have no reason to keep it, and many privacy-minded people disable it.
- **Battery and data.** It is usually light, but any background process uses some of both.
- **Control.** Software you cannot uninstall is something people understandably object to.


Check Meta's Help Center and your phone maker's documentation for the specific behavior on your model, because it varies by device and version.


## How to disable it


Exact menus differ by phone brand. The steps below fit most Android phones.


1. Open **Settings** and go to **Apps** (sometimes Apps and notifications).
2. Choose to see all apps, and turn on the option to show system apps if the list is empty.
3. Find **Meta App Manager** . You may also see Meta Services and Meta App Installer.
4. Tap **Uninstall** if it is offered. If you only see **Disable** , tap that.
5. Confirm. If the button is greyed out, your phone locks the app, and you can instead restrict its background activity and permissions.


After disabling, check that Facebook, Messenger and Instagram still open and update in the Play Store. For nearly everyone, they do.


## What happens if you disable it


- Meta apps already on your phone keep working.
- Updates come from the Google Play Store instead. If an app was only ever updated through Meta App Manager, you may see it fall behind, in which case update it from the Play Store or reinstall.
- If you use no Meta apps at all, nothing changes.


You can re-enable it at any time in the same list.


## Related names you may see


Meta's name appears on several different things, and mixing them up leads to wrong fixes:


- **Meta Business Suite:** a tool for managing Facebook and Instagram Pages, posts and messages from one inbox.
- **Meta Business Manager, now Business Portfolio:** where a company keeps its Pages, ad accounts, pixels and the people who can access them.
- **Meta Pixel:** a snippet on a website that reports visitor actions back to Meta. See the guide to the[Meta Pixel Helper](https://www.sprites.ai/blog/meta-pixel-helper-chrome-extension) .
- **Meta Ad Library:** the public archive of ads. Nothing to do with your phone.


Of everything named here, only Meta App Manager runs on your phone, and only on some Android devices.


## Meta App Manager vs Meta Ads Manager


These two share a company name and nothing else. The mix-up is common because they sound alike.


Meta App Manager Meta Ads Manager


What it is An Android system app on your phone A web tool (and mobile app) for running ads


Who uses it Nobody directly. It runs in the background Advertisers and agencies


What it does Installs and updates Meta's apps Builds campaigns, sets budgets, reads results


Where to find it Settings, Apps Through your Meta Business account


If your goal is running ads, you want Ads Manager, and the guides to[Facebook ads cost](https://www.sprites.ai/blog/facebook-ads-cost) and[the Meta pixel and Conversions API](https://www.sprites.ai/blog/shopify-meta-pixel) are the better starting places. There is also a third thing with a similar name: Meta Business Suite, which handles posts and messages for Pages and Instagram accounts.


## If you came here for ads research


Many people search Meta's product names while trying to see what competitors advertise. That is a different tool again, the Meta Ad Library. It is a free public archive. The[Meta ads library](https://www.sprites.ai/meta-ads-library) hub on Sprites groups Facebook and Instagram ads by brand and category, with pages such as[Nike ads](https://www.sprites.ai/nike-ads) and[Allbirds ads](https://www.sprites.ai/allbirds-ads) . The step-by-step version is in[how to see competitors' Facebook ads](https://www.sprites.ai/blog/how-to-see-competitors-facebook-ads) .

It has no connection to anything on your phone. See[pricing](https://www.sprites.ai/pricing) .


## Frequently asked questions


### What is Meta App Manager?


It is an Android system app from Meta that installs and updates Meta apps such as Facebook, Messenger and Instagram. It was previously named Facebook App Manager.


### Is Meta App Manager a virus?


No. It is genuine Meta software, preinstalled by phone makers and carriers. Some people still disable it for privacy or because it runs in the background.


### Can I uninstall Meta App Manager?


Often not. Many phones only let you disable it. Go to Settings, Apps, show system apps, find it and tap Disable or Uninstall, whichever appears.


### What happens if I disable Meta App Manager?


Your Meta apps keep working and update through the Google Play Store. If you use none of them, you will notice nothing.


### Is Meta App Manager the same as Meta Ads Manager?


No. App Manager is a background app on Android phones. Ads Manager is the tool advertisers use to create and measure ads on Facebook and Instagram.


### Why is Meta App Manager on my phone if I never installed it?


Your phone maker or carrier preinstalled it as part of an agreement with Meta. Not every phone has it, and iPhones do not.
